evals.prompt: How do I make sure our SaaS product shows up in AI search results? We're a project management tool and we keep getting left out of ChatGPT and Perplexity recommendations when people ask about project management software.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing-context.md first. Should establish a Visibility Baseline across platforms (Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity). Should apply the unified audit framework where relevant: On-Page & Structural Optimization (content extractability, clear definitions, comparison tables), Content Quality & Authority (statistics, citations, expert attribution), Off-Site Presence (Wikipedia, Reddit, review sites), and Machine-Readability (schema, /pricing.md). Should reference Princeton GEO research findings (citations improve visibility +40%, statistics +37%). Should check AI bot access in robots.txt. Should provide a prioritized action plan.
assertions: Establishes a Visibility Baseline across AI platforms
Applies relevant framework steps (On-Page & Structural, Content Quality & Authority, Off-Site Presence)
Checks AI bot access in robots.txt

evals.prompt: Should we block AI crawlers like GPTBot and PerplexityBot in our robots.txt? We're worried about content theft.
evals.expected_output: Should address the AI bot access question directly under Crawlability & Indexation. Should explain the tradeoff: blocking AI bots prevents training on your content but also prevents AI platforms from citing and recommending you. Should reference the specific bots and their purposes (GPTBot, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, etc.). Should provide the recommended robots.txt configuration (or point to references/platform-ranking-factors.md for the full config). Should explain that blocking may hurt AI visibility more than it protects content, and mention CCBot as a safe-to-block training-only exception. Should give a nuanced recommendation based on business goals.
assertions: Explains impact on AI visibility vs content protection
Lists specific AI bot user agents
Provides or references the recommended robots.txt configuration
Mentions CCBot as a safe-to-block training-only exception
Gives nuanced recommendation based on business goals

evals.prompt: What kind of content gets cited most by AI systems? We want to create content specifically optimized for AI search.
evals.expected_output: Should reference the 'Content Types That Win Both Ways' table, including comparisons (~33% of AI citations), definitive guides (~15%), and other high-citation content types. Should explain why these formats work (structured, extractable, authoritative). Should provide specific recommendations: clear definitions, structured data, original statistics, comparison tables, expert quotes. Should reference the Princeton GEO research on what increases citation probability, and may point to references/content-patterns.md for block templates.
assertions: References specific content types with citation rates
Explains why these formats work for AI
Mentions structured data, statistics, and clear definitions

Should recommend specific content structure changes and a monitoring approach.
assertions: Focuses on Google AI Overviews specifically
Explains how AI Overviews selects sources
Checks On-Page & Structural Optimization (extractability, headings, answer-first)

evals.prompt: Our organic search traffic has dropped 30% this quarter. Can you do a full SEO audit to figure out what's going on?
evals.expected_output: Should treat this as a standard traffic-drop diagnostic and run the unified audit framework directly, in priority order, without deferring to any other skill: Crawlability & Indexation (deindexation, robots.txt changes, sitemap issues), Technical Foundations (Core Web Vitals regressions), On-Page & Structural Optimization, and Content Quality & Authority (content decay, E-E-A-T). Should investigate timing against known algorithm updates. May note AI Overview changes as a contributing factor if relevant, but should prioritize traditional ranking/indexation causes first since no AI-specific symptom was mentioned. Should provide an Executive Summary and a prioritized action plan.
assertions: Runs the unified audit framework directly rather than deferring to another skill
Follows priority order: crawlability first, then technical, on-page, content
May mention AI Overview changes as a contributing factor without over-indexing on it
Provides Executive Summary and prioritized action plan

evals.prompt: Can you do an SEO audit of our SaaS website? We're getting about 2,000 organic visits/month but feel like we should be getting more. URL: https://example.com
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing-context.md first. Should ask clarifying questions about priority keywords, Search Console access, recent changes, and competitors. Should follow the unified audit framework priority order: Crawlability & Indexation, Technical Foundations, On-Page & Structural Optimization, Content Quality & Authority, Off-Site Presence, Machine-Readability. Should check robots.txt, XML sitemap, site architecture. Should evaluate title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure, and content optimization. Should NOT report on schema markup based solely on web_fetch (must note the detection limitation). assertions: Asks clarifying questions about keywords, Search Console, recent changes
Follows unified audit priority order: crawlability first, then technical, on-page, content, off-site, machine-readability
Evaluates title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure
Does NOT claim 'no schema found' based on web_fetch alone
Each finding has Issue, Impact, Evidence, Fix, and Priority

evals.prompt: Why am I not ranking for 'project management software'? We have a page targeting that keyword but it's stuck on page 3.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on the casual 'why am I not ranking' phrasing. Should investigate both on-page and off-page factors. On-page: check title tag, H1, URL alignment with keyword; evaluate content depth vs competitors; check for keyword cannibalization. Technical: check indexation status, canonical tags, crawlability. Content quality: assess E-E-A-T signals, content depth, user engagement. Should provide specific, actionable fixes organized by priority. Should mention competitive analysis against current top-ranking pages.
assertions: Triggers on casual 'why am I not ranking' phrasing
Checks title tag, H1, URL alignment with target keyword
Checks indexation status and canonical tags
Mentions competitive analysis against top-ranking pages
Provides actionable fixes organized by priority

evals.prompt: We just migrated from WordPress to Next.js and our organic traffic dropped 40% in the last month. Help!
evals.expected_output: Should treat this as an urgent migration diagnostic. Should immediately check: redirect mapping (301s from old URLs to new), canonical tags on new pages, robots.txt not blocking crawlers, XML sitemap submitted and updated, meta tags preserved. Should check for common migration issues: redirect chains/loops, soft 404s, lost internal links, changed URL structures without redirects. Should reference Search Console coverage report for indexation issues. Should provide a prioritized recovery plan with critical fixes first. Should mention monitoring timeline expectations (recovery can take weeks).
assertions: Checks canonical tags on new pages
Checks XML sitemap updated and submitted
Checks for redirect chains or loops

evals.prompt: Review the technical SEO of our e-commerce site. We have about 50,000 products and use faceted navigation.
evals.expected_output: Should focus on e-commerce-specific technical issues: faceted navigation creating duplicate content, crawl budget management for large product catalog, parameterized URLs, product schema markup (with the caveat about detection limitations). Should check for thin category pages, duplicate product descriptions, out-of-stock page handling. Should address crawl budget issues: pagination, infinite scroll handling, session IDs in URLs. Should provide structured findings with Impact ratings and specific fixes.
assertions: Addresses crawl budget for large catalog
Mentions product schema with detection limitation caveat
Findings include Impact ratings and specific fixes

evals.prompt: Can you check our blog posts for on-page SEO issues? We publish 4 posts per week but traffic has been flat for 6 months.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Blog / Content Sites playbook: check for outdated content not refreshed, keyword cannibalization, missing topical clustering, poor internal linking, missing author pages. Should audit on-page elements: title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure, keyword targeting per post. Should assess E-E-A-T signals for blog content. Should check for content depth issues and whether posts answer search intent. Should recommend a content audit process and provide a prioritized action plan for the existing content library.
assertions: Checks for author pages and E-E-A-T signals
Audits title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure
Assesses whether content answers search intent

evals.prompt: I run a local plumbing business with 3 locations. My website barely shows up when people search for 'plumber near me' in our areas. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Local Business playbook. Should check for: inconsistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) across the site, missing local schema markup (with detection limitation caveat), Google Business Profile optimization, missing individual location pages for each of the 3 locations, and missing local content. Should also check standard technical and on-page factors. Should recommend local-specific fixes: location-specific pages with unique content, local schema on each, GBP optimization, citation consistency.
assertions: Checks for local schema markup with detection caveat
Recommends individual location pages for each location
Checks standard technical SEO factors too
Provides prioritized local SEO action plan

evals.prompt: Our site loads really slowly, especially on mobile. Pages take 5-6 seconds to load. Is this hurting our SEO?
evals.expected_output: Should focus on the Technical Foundations framework step. Should explain CWV thresholds: LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1, and that 5-6s load time is well above acceptable. Should investigate speed factors: server response time (TTFB), image optimization, JavaScript execution, CSS delivery, caching headers, CDN usage, font loading. Should recommend specific tools: PageSpeed Insights, WebPageTest, Chrome DevTools, Search Console CWV report. Should confirm page speed impacts both traditional rankings and AI platforms (Copilot explicitly favors sub-2s load times). Should provide prioritized fixes.
assertions: Confirms page speed impacts both traditional rankings and AI platform citation
